Pull the study results of one or more JATOS batches

Source: R/rawdata-jatos.R
pull_jatos_batches.Rd

Downloads every study result of the listed batches through {jatosR} and binds them into one table. The connection is tested first, so a wrong token fails before any batch is requested. Batch that cannot be pulled is named in the error.

Usage

pull_jatos_batches(url, batch_ids, token, result_file = NULL)

Arguments

url

Character(1). Address of the JATOS server, e.g. "https://jatos.mindprobe.eu".

batch_ids

Integer-valued numeric vector of JATOS batch IDs, without duplicates.

token

Character(1). A JATOS API token, "jap_..." with or without the "Bearer " prefix. Read it from .Renviron rather than typing it into a script, e.g. Sys.getenv("mindprobe_catlas_token").

result_file

NULL (default) or Character(1). Name of a JATOS result file that holds the complete data of a study result, e.g. "jspsych-data.json" from fba-allergy-online-02 on. NULL reads the streamed data only, as for builds that upload no result file (e.g. fba-allergy-online-01). See details.

Value

A tibble with one row per JATOS study result, including the columns of jatosR::process_results()$data (among them id_sr, id_cr, batch_id, start_date_sr, study_state and data_raw), jatos_study_id representing the JATOS study each batch belongs to, and data_source, the source of data_raw: "file" (the result file), "stream" (the streamed data) or NA (neither exists). The time the pull finished, in UTC, is attached as the attribute "retrieved_at", ready for build_provenance().

Details

Batches may belong to different JATOS studies, for instance when a study was re-deployed after a patch. jatos_study_id keeps this fact visible.

Result files

CATLAS experiments stream every trial to JATOS as it finishes, and from fba-allergy-online-02 on they also upload the complete jsPsych data as a result file at the end of the run. A trial whose upload failed, e.g. during a dropped internet connection, is missing from the streamed data but present in the file. With result_file given, the file of every study result is requested from the JATOS API (/jatos/api/v1/results/files/, JATOS 3.8.1 and later), and the following rule applies:

  • Where the file exists, it is read instead of the streamed data. The two are never combined, because the file of a finished run repeats every streamed trial.

  • Where it does not exist (unfinished runs, failed uploads), the streamed data are read.

  • Where it exists but does not parse, the streamed data are read, with a warning.

Where both exist, the file must hold every streamed trial apart from email-collection records, matched on trial_index. A file that does not is still read, with a warning naming the affected study result. Every call reports how many study results were read from each source, names those read from the streamed data, and counts the trials recovered from the files.

See also

parse_jatos_results(), repair_jatos_json()
